d: When offered a known reinforcing item or activity, the student will take/use the item or activity.
t: 1 = either not all the time or takes more than 3 seconds to respond
2 = takes within 3 seconds all the time

d: When offered one reinforcing item or activity and another non-reinforcing item or activity, the student will select the reinforcing item or activity.
t: 1 = either not all the time or takes more than 3 seconds to respond
2 = takes within 3 seconds all the time

d: Student will look at and track changes in location of a non-reinforcing item presented by an instructor.
t: 1 = will look at item but requires an additional prompt to look or takes more than 3 seconds to respond
2 = finds it in any position (up/down/left/right) within 3 seconds
3 = will track the movement of the item to 4 positions in 10 seconds
4 = will track the movement of the item to 6 different positions in a 10 second period

d: When offered a common object, the student will take the item.
t: 1 = either not all the time or takes more than 3 seconds to respond
2 = takes within 3 seconds all the time

d: When a specific tangible reinforcer is available and there is a clearly identified requirement for a known response to be performed, the student will approach the instructor and perform the required response (i.e., the student knows that there is a reinforcer available but that he will need to approach the instructor and do a simple task to get the reinforcer).
t: 1 = will occasionally approach and perform at least one response for the reinforcer
2 = will readily and repeatedly approach and perform a variety of known single responses
3 = will approach and perform multiple responses (each response is reinforced)
4 = will approach and sit at a table and perform multiple responses to get reinforcers (each response is reinforced)

d: The student will work for instructor controlled reinforcement.
t: 1 = 3 maintenance responses for 3 presentations
2 = 5 maintenance responses for 5 presentations
3 = 2 acquisition & 3 maintenance responses for 5 presentations
4 = engages in 5 acquisition responses for at least 5 presentations of a particular reinforcer

d: The student will be able to demonstrate and use skills learned with one instructor when working with other instructors.
t: 1 = works readily with 3 or more instructors at about the same rate and quality of responding
2 = works readily with 3 or more instructors and with novel instructors at about the same rate and quality of responding demonstrated with familiar instructors

d: When an instructor is attempting to engage the student in learning activities (at a table, while seated on the floor, or standing near materials for an activity), the student will wait calmly, remain generally oriented towards the instructor and materials, and will keep his hands away from the instructional materials until an instruction is presented.
t: 1 = requires only one prompt to sit/stand nicely or keep hands off the materials
2 = while sitting or standing in front of task materials the student consistently waits calmly orienting towards the materials without requiring prompts to leave the materials alone

d: When engaged in an obvious series of learning tasks, the student will scan the materials and look at the instructor to seek the instruction for the next task.
t: 1 = after scanning materials, student requires only one prompt to orient to the instructor for an instruction to be presented
2 = after scanning materials, student consistently looks to the instructor for the next instruction

d: When an instruction is presented during a series of learning tasks that involve instructional materials, the student will attend to the instruction then scan the materials prior to responding to the instruction.
t: 1 = can consistently scan up to 3 task-related items within 3 seconds (prior to responding)
2 = can consistently scan up to 6 task-related items within 3 seconds (prior to responding)

d: When engaged in a series of learning tasks, the student will respond quickly when an instruction is presented.
t: 1 = consistently responds within 5 seconds when instructions are presented
2 = consistently responds within 3 seconds when instructions are presented

d: A variety of items and activities serve as reinforcers.
t: 1 = at least 5 items or activities are effective as reinforcers
2 = at least 10 separate instructor controllable items or activities are effective as reinforcers for learning behaviors

d: The student will work for intermittent reinforcement.
t: 1 = 2 maintenance responses for an edible or tangible reinforcer
2 = 4 maintenance responses for an edible or tangible reinforcer
3 = 2 acquisition and 3 maintenance responses for a reinforcer
4 = engages in 5 acquisition responses for an edible or tangible reinforcer

d: The student will work for reinforcement that involves fun interaction with the instructor.
t: 1 = 2 maintenance responses for instructor interaction reinforcer
2 = 4 maintenance responses for instructor interaction
3 = 2 acquisition and 3 maintenance responses for instructor interaction
4 = engages in 5 acquisition responses for instructor interaction reinforcer

d: After completing a task, when engaged in a series of learning activities, the student will orient to the instructor such as to observe the changes in instructor's facial expression and voice that provide feedback regarding the correctness of the response.
t: 1 = occasionally looks at instructors to seek feedback when finished responding (without the instructor using highly exaggerated changes in behavior to get the student to notice)
2 = looks at instructors to seek feedback when finished responding at least 70% of the time

d: Praise will serve as an effective reinforcer for the student.
t: 1 = works for praise for 3 responses prior to receiving a back-up reinforcer
2 = works for praise for 5 minutes with back-up reinforcer
3 = works for praise for 15 minutes with a back-up reinforcer
4 = works for 15 minutes for only praise

d: The student will be able to wait appropriately if a reinforcer is not delivered immediately following a behavior.
t: 1 = 5 seconds
2 = 10 seconds
3 = 1 minute
4 = waits 5 minutes

d: The student will seek recognition for his accomplishments.
t: 1 = looks to see if others have noticed what they have done
2 = asks others to see what they have done

d: Completion of a task serves as an effective reinforcer for the student.
t: 1 = works independently for 5 minutes to complete a task with only praise as the reinforcer
2 = works independently 10 minutes to complete task for recognition of task completion

d: When given single, uniquely shaped pieces from an inset puzzle; the student will put the puzzle pieces into the puzzle frame.
t: 1 = places up to 3 pieces handed separately using trial and error
2 = 5 pieces handed separately using trial and error
3 = 3 pieces presented as group by looking and positioning
4 = places 5 pieces presented as group by looking and positioning

d: When provided a form box shape sorter and its pieces, the student will be able to put the pieces into the corresponding holes in the form box.
t: 1 = 2 pieces by trial and error
2 = 4 pieces using trial and error approach
3 = 4 pieces by look and locate
4 = 6 pieces by looking at piece then visually locating the corresponding hole

d: When given an object the student will match to an identical object in an array of three items.
t: 1 = can match one objet to an identical object in a display of 2 items
2 = at least two objects to objects in a display of 2 items
3 = at least 5 objects to objects in a display of 4 items
4 = at least 10 objects to objects in a display of 8 items

d: When given an item, the student will match the object to one of three pictures in an array.
t: 1 = can match a single item per task presentation
2 = can match three items in succession

d: When given a picture, the student will match to an identical picture in an array of three pictures.
t: 1 = can match one picture to an identical picture in a display of 2 pictures
2 = at least two pictures to pictures in a display of 2
3 = at least 5 pictures to pictures in a display of 4
4 = at least 10 pictures to pictures in a display of 8 pictures

d: When given a picture of an item, the student will match the picture to one of three objects in an array.
t: 1 = can match a single item per task presentation
2 = can match three items in succession

d: When given a group of ten pictures of items, the student will match those pictures to an identical picture in an array of ten pictures in quick succession.
t: 1 = can match 5 separate items in 15 seconds
2 = can match at least 10 items in 30 seconds

d: When given a variety of nonidentical objects or pictures representing three items, and given an array of sample items for each of the three items, the student will sort nonidentical items into the appropriate groups (e.g., all the dogs, all the trees, all the people).
t: 1 = given 4 items (2 of each 2 items), can sort 2 types of items into an array of 2 samples
2 = given 6 items (2 each of 3 items), can sort at least 4 types of items into array of 3 samples
3 = given 12 items (3 each of 4 items), can sort at least 6 types of items into array of 4 samples
4 = given 20 items (5 each of 4 items), can sort 10 or more types of items into an array of 4 samples

d: When given a block design card, student will place the blocks in the appropriate location on the design card disregarding extra blocks.
t: 1 = can do designs using 2 blocks (no extras)
2 = can do up to 4 blocks (no extras)
3 = 4 or more blocks (some extras)
4 = can quickly complete designs with 6 or more blocks (some extras)

d: When given uniquely-shaped, connecting puzzle pieces which fit into an irregularly shaped inset frame, the student will complete the puzzle.
t: 1 = 1 puzzle with at least 5 pieces
2 = 2 puzzles with 5 pieces
3 = 4 puzzles with 5 pieces
4 = 4 puzzles with 8 pieces

d: When given a square-edged framed puzzle, the student will complete the puzzle.
t: 1 = 3 puzzles with at least 2 pieces
2 = 3 puzzles with 3 pieces
3 = 3 puzzles with 4 pieces
4 = 3 puzzles with 5 pieces

d: When given a block design card, student will place blocks to make the design shown on the card.
t: 1 = can do designs using 2 blocks (no extra blocks)
2 = can do up to 4 pieces (no extras)
3 = 4 or more parts (extras)
4 = can quickly complete designs with 6 or more pieces (some extra blocks)

d: When given a visual sequence pattern consisting of items (e.g., colored blocks) the student will arrange items to match the pattern.
t: 1 = 6 pieces of two items with no extras
2 = 6 pieces of three items with on extras
3 = 8 pieces of 4 items with no extras
4 = can match sequence of 8 pieces comprised of 4 different items when given extra pieces

d: When given irregularly-shaped, non-interlocking puzzle pieces, student will correctly juxtapose the pieces to form a picture.
t: 1 = 1 puzzle with at least 3 pieces
2 = 2 puzzles with 3 pieces
3 = 4 puzzles with 4 pieces
4 = 4 puzzles with 5 pieces

d: When given a standard jigsaw puzzle (interlocking pieces without a frame), the student will correctly complete the puzzle.
t: 1 = one puzzle with at least 8 pieces
2 = two puzzles with 8 pieces
3 = 2 puzzles with 12 pieces
4 = at least four puzzles with 12 pieces

d: Given an array of items or pictures, the student will be able to match an item that is associated with one of the items in the array (e.g., match a bat to picture of a ball).
t: 1 = can match at least 1 related picture for 5 items
2 = 1 related picture for 10 items
3 = 2 related pictures for 10 items
4 = can match at least 2 related pictures for 20 or more items

d: When provided with a sample of two items that have different functions and shown a demonstrations of matching another items that has the same function, the student will be able to sort additional pictures that have the same functions with the correct samples items.
t: 1 = at least 2 items from 2 functions
2 = at least 5 items from 2 functions
3 = at least 5 items from 3 functions
4 = at least 5 items from 4 functions

d: When provided with a sample of two items that have different features/parts and shown a demonstrations of matching another item that has the same feature/part, the student will be able to sort additional pictures that have the same features/parts with the correct samples items.
t: 1 = at least 2 items from 2 features/parts
2 = at least 5 items from 2 features/parts
3 = at least 5 items from 3 features/parts
4 = at least 5 items from 4 features/parts

d: When provided with a sample of three different classes of items and shown a demonstration of matching another member of each class, the student will be able to sort additional pictures that match the class to which the item belongs.
t: 1 = at least 2 items from 2 classes
2 = at least 5 items from 2 classes
3 = at least 5 items from 3 classes
4 = at least 5 items from 4 classes

d: After having been shown a model of items in a specific sequence and then having the model removed, the student will be able to replicate the sequence.
t: 1 = two items with 2 second delay with only verbal or gestural prompts
2 = two items in two seconds without prompts
3 = three items with two second delay or two items with 5 second delay
4 = immediately, with three items after 5 second delay

d: When shown a specific item and it is removed, and five items are then presented (one being the same as the original item), the student will be able to find the initial item.
t: 1 = after 2 second day, can find any one of 3 items within 3 seconds, when presented an array of 2 items
2 = after 3 second delay, can find any one of 5 items within 3 seconds, when presented an array of 3 items
3 = after 3 second delay, can find any one of 5 items within 3 seconds
4 = after 5 second delay, can find any one of 10 items within 3 seconds, when presented an array of 5 items

d: When given a model of items in a specific sequence (regular and irregular), the student will be able to continue adding items in the correct sequence (e.g., ABABAB, ABCABC, ABBABB, AABAAB, ABBCABBC).
t: 1 = two items in an alternating sequence
2 = three items in a regular sequence
3 = three items in a regular sequence with extra irrelevant pieces present
4 = continues an irregular pattern with at least 3 different stimuli with irrelevant pieces present

d: Given a set of blocks or other items and a model of a simple 3-dimensional object (e.g., a house, car), the student will be able to arrange the blocks or other items to replicate the structure.
t: 1 = can replicate 2 objects using at least 3 blocks or other items
2 = can replicate 2 objects using at least 6 blocks or other items

d: The student will be able to observe a person placing multiple identical objects on a table and then place a different item on each of those items immediately after each one of the first type of item has been placed.
t: 1 = can immediately place an item on a corresponding item for a series of at least 3 responses
2 = can immediately place an items on a corresponding item for a series of at least 6 responses

d: When given a model of the start and end of continuum, student will be able to arrange additional task stimuli in the appropriate order by size, quantity, shade of color, and sequence.
t: 1 = two sets of items for one attribute
2 = two sets of items for two attributes
3 = two sets of items for three attributes
4 = can arrange at least four sets of items for each of the four specified attributes

d: The student will be able to arrange a set of picture cards in the appropriate sequence.
t: 1 = the two sets of items with a three-card sequence
2 = three sets of items with a three-card sequence
3 = five sets of items with a three-card sequence
4 = can arrange at least five sets of four items in a sequence

d: The student will be able to draw a line from the start to the end of simple mazes.
t: 1 = can draw a line in a maze which has only 1 choice point for selecting the correct path
2 = can draw a line from start to end in a maze which has 3 choice points for selecting the correct path

d: Student will look at or come to a person when called by his name.
t: 1 = requires some prompts to respond
2 = looks or comes at least 80% of the time

d: When given instructions to do a preferred. activity in the context of the ongoing activity, the student will comply with the instructions.
t: 1 = 3 or more activities with only partial physical prompts
2 = 3 or more activities with a model and no physical prompts
3 = at least 3 activities with only one additional verbal or pointing prompt
4 = at least 3 activities without prompts

d: Upon request, student quill look at a reinforcing item held by an instructor.
t: 1 = will look at item but requires an additional prompt to look or takes more than 3 seconds to respond
2 = looks at it in any position (up/down/left/right) within 3 seconds

d: Upon instruction, the student will touch a preferred item held in various positions.
t: 1 = touches or grabs an item within 3 seconds if it is held in front of him
2 = readily touches an item in any position (up/down/left/right) within 3 seconds

d: Upon instruction, the student will touch a common item held in various positions.
t: 1 = touches or grabs an item within 3 seconds if it is held in front of him
2 = readily touches an item in any position (up/down/left/right) within 3 seconds

d: The student will comply with instructions to do a preferred activity even though it is not occurring at that time.
t: 1 = 3 or more activities with only partial physical prompts
2 = 3 or more with a model and no physical prompts
3 = at least 3 with only one verbal or pointing prompt
4 = at least 3 activities without prompts

d: The students will comply with the instructions to do a non-preferred activity when the activity is presently occurring.
t: 1 = 3 or more activities with only partial physical prompts
2 = 3 or more with a model and no physical prompts
3 = at least 3 with only one verbal or pointing prompt
4 = at least 3 activities without prompts

d: The student will follow instructions which require him to give a named, non-reinforcing item.
t: 1 = usually with one additional prompt (not including holding out hand to receive the item)
2 = usually within 3 seconds

d: The student will comply with instructions to do a simple motor task (e.g., clap, turn around, arms up).
t: 1 = at least 2 instructions without prompts
2 = at least 4 instructions without prompts
3 = at least 6 instructions without prompts
4 = at least 6 instructions without prompts and can follow at least 4 different actions within 10 seconds

d: When asked to touch an object that is being held and an empty hand is held out as a distracter (or the object is placed on a table with another neutral item such a styrofoam cube used as a distracter), the student will touch the named object.
t: 1 = touches an item if it is held in front of him
2 = readily finds and touches it in any position within 3 seconds

d: When asked, the student will select a named reinforcing item from an array of two objects held or placed in any of position in front of him.
t: 1 = finds and selects item if it is held in front of him
2 = readily finds and selects it in any position within 3 seconds

d: Upon request, the student will be able to select an object named by the instructor from an array of two reinforcing objects held or placed in any position in front of him.
t: 1 = finds and selects item if it is held in front of him
2 = readily finds and selects it in any position within 3 seconds

d: Upon request, the student will be able to select an object named by the instructor from an array of two common objects held or placed in any position in front of him.
t: 1 = identifies at least 2 objects
2 = 10 objects
3 = identifies at least one example of 25 objects
4 = receptively identifies 50 or more objects and can identify several different examples of most of those objects

d: Upon request, student will select a picture named by the instructor from an array of two pictures of common items held or placed in any position in front of him.
t: 1 = 2 pictures
2 = 10 pictures
3 = 25 pictures of different items
4 = receptively identifies pictures of 50 or more items and can identify several different pictures of most of those items

d: The student will be able to follow directions to touch parts  of his own body.
t: 1 = 2 parts
2 = 4 parts
3 = 6 parts
4 = 10 or more parts

d: The student will select a specified object for at least 100 common objects when the object is presented in an array of six or more objects on a table in any position in front of the student.
t: 1 = 5 objects when presented in an array of three objects
2 = 10 objects (array of 3)
3 = 50 objects of at least one example of the item when presented in an array of three objects
4 = receptively identifies 100 or more objects and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those objects when presented in an array of six or more objects

d: The student will select a specified picture for at least 100 common objects when the picture is presented in an array of six or more pictures on a table in any position in front of the student.
t: 1 = 5 pictures when presented in an array of three or more pictures
2 = 10 pictures (array of 3)
3 = 50 pictures of at least one example of the item when presented in an array of three or more pictures
4 = receptively identifies 100 or more pictures and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those pictures when presented in an array of six or more pictures

d: The student will be able to acquire selection skills for many new common objects or pictures of items after being required to select the items less than five times.
t: 1 = selects many new items after being required to select the items less than 10 times
2 = readily learns to select many new items after being required to select the items less than 5 times

d: The student will be able to point to or select known items from an array upon request when presented in quick succession.
t: 1 = can point to or select 5 separate known items in 15 seconds
2 = can sequentially point to or select at least 10 known items in 30 seconds

d: The student will be able to select objects and pictures named by the instructor while using a variety of instructions to select those items (e.g."Show me _." "Where is the _." "Can you find the _." "Touch the _.").
t: 1 = selects objects and pictures when given any 2 instructions to select a specified item (can use any response)
2 = selects objects and pictures when given any of 5 instructions to select a specified item (any selection response is acceptable)

d: The student will be able to follow directions to point to body parts of other people or touch pictures of body parts.
t: 1 = 2 parts
2 = 4 parts
3 = 6 parts
4 = 10 or more parts

d: The student will be able to follow directions to touch clothing items on his own body.
t: 1 = 2 items
2 = 4 or more items

d: The student will be able to follow directions to touch specified parts of items (e.g., door and window of a house, wheel and door of a car).
t: 1 = at least 2 parts of two objects
2 = 2 pars of four objects
3 = 3 parts of six objects
4 = 3 or more parts of ten objects

d: The student will be able to select between two similar items that vary on one dimension (i.e., adjectives).
t: 1 = can identify at least one adjective
2 = at least 5 adjectives (may be all colors)
3 = at least 10 adjectives (at least 5 of which are not colors)
4 = selects at least 20 adjectives (including at least 3 colors, 2 shapes and 2 sizes)

d: The student will be able to select an item by attending to the eye orientation of another person.
t: 1 = can select one of two separated items located on a table
2 = can select one of three separated items located on a table

d: The student will be able to follow hand signals from an adult to come, sit, stand, go to a location, and perform an action when signaled (e.g., stand up or clap hands when point to the child).
t: 1 = can respond to at least 2 types of hand signals
2 = can respond correctly to at least 3 types of hand signals
3 = can respond correctly to at least 4 types of hand signals
4 = can respond correctly to all 5 types of hand signals

d: Student will be able to walk across the room to go to a specified person.
t: 1 = can go to at least two people upon request
2 = can go to at least four people upon request

d: Student will be able to walk across the room to go to a specified place or person and place or deliver an item (e.g., give pen to Jim).
t: 1 = 1 person or place with only a verbal prompt
2 = 2 people or places with only a single verbal prompt
3 = 2 people or places without prompts
4 = can go to at least 2 people and 2 places and deliver/place a given item

d: Student will be able to walk across the room to go to a specified place or person and get a requested item.
t: 1 = 1 person or place with only a verbal prompt
2 = 2 people or places with only a single verbal prompt
3 = 2 people or places without prompts
4 = can go to at least 2 people and 2 places and get a specified item

d: Student will be able to walk across the room to go to a specified person and perform a stated action (e.g., give Jim a hug).
t: 1 = 1 person and 1 action
2 = 2 people and 1 action
3 = 2 people and 2 actions
4 = can go to at least three people and perform at least 2 actions

d: The student will select common objects and pictures with a specific motor response when given a variety of instructions specifying the response required to select those items (e.g., "Touch," "Point to," "Give me," "Pick up," "Get the").
t: 1 = two different selection responses
2 = three different selection responses
3 = four different selection responses
4 = responds correctly to any of 5 different selection responses

d: The student will comply with instructions to do a simple action when presented with several objects, one of which is used to perform the action.
t: 1 = at least 2 with only verbal or pointing prompts
2 = at least 5 without prompts

d: The student will be able to perform a specified action with a specific object, when several different objects are present that could be used to demonstrate the requested action.
t: 1 = can perform 2 actions on at least 2 objects
2 = can perform at least 2 actions on 4 objects
3 = can perform at least 3 actions on 4 objects
4 = can perform at least 4 actions on at least 4 objects

d: The student will comply with instructions to do a pretend activity.
t: 1 = at least 2 with only verbal or pointing prompts
2 = at least 5 without prompts

d: Upon the request, the student will select a specified action picture from an array of three pictures on a table in any position in front of the student.
t: 1 = 2 action pictures
2 = 5 actions
3 = 10 actions
4 = selects 20 or more action pictures and can identify several different examples (including novel examples) of most of those actions

d: Given an array of items or pictures and asked, "What goes with this?," the student will be able to select the item which is used with the item being shown (e.g., select a bat when shown a picture of a ball).
t: 1 = can select at least 1 related picture for 5 items
2 = 1 related picture for 10 items
3 = 2 related pictures for 10 items
4 = can select at least 2 related pictures for 20 or more items

d: Student will be able to select objects or pictures of items when told the item's function.
t: 1 = at least 2 items
2 = at least 5
3 = at least 25 items
4 = can select at least 25 items when told the item's function and can select 2 or more items with a specified function from a display of at least 6 items

d: Student will be able to select objects or pictures of items when told the item's features or parts.
t: 1 = at least 1 feature or part for 2 items
2 = at least 1 feature or part for 5 items
3 = at least 2 features or parts for 25 items
4 = can select at least 2 features or parts for 25 items and can select 2 or more items with a specified feature/part from a display of at least 6 items

d: Student will be able to select objects or pictures of items when told the class to which the item belongs.
t: 1 = at least 5 items from 1 class
2 = at least 5 items from 2 classes
3 = at least 5 items from 4 classes
4 = can select at least 5 items from 4 classes and can select 2 or more items of a specified class from a display of at least 6 items

d: Upon request, the student will select two specified objects or pictures from a larger selection of objects on a table in front of the student.
t: 1 = can select 2 specified objects or pictures when given a display of at least 4 items
2 = can select 2 specified objects or pictures when given a display of 10 or more items

d: Upon request, the student will select two specified objects or  pictures, in the order requested, from a larger selection of pictures on a table in front of the student.
t: 1 = can select 2 specified items in order when given a display of at least 4 pictures
2 = can select 2 specified items in order when given a display of 10 or more pictures

d: The student will be able to select pictures of common community helpers in his environment.
t: 1 = 1 community helper
2 = 2 community helpers
3 = 3 community helpers
4 = selects 4 or more community helpers

d: The student will be able to locate pictures of objects within a larger, complex picture.
t: 1 = can find at least 2 of 4 items in a display which contains at least 5 other items
2 = can find at least 3 of 4 items in a display which contains at least 10 other items

d: The student will be able to locate objects when only shown parts of the objects within a larger, complex picture.
t: 1 = can find at least 2 of 4 items in a display which contains at least 5 other items
2 = can find at least 3 of 4 items in a display which contains at least 10 other items

d: The student will select appropriate pictures when the sound which is paired with that item is heard.
t: 1 = at least 2 sounds
2 = at least 4 sounds
3 = at least 6 sounds
4 = at least 8 sounds

d: The student will be able to follow directions to select all the examples of a specified item (e.g., all the cats).
t: 1 = at least 2 similar items from a total array of at least four items
2 = 3 items from an array of at least six items
3 = 3 items from an array of ten items
4 = 6 similar items from a total array of at least fifteen items

d: Given a scene or a varied set of objects or pictures, the student will be able to select a specified item which has the two specified characteristics (e.g., "The big red ball," "The hot breakfast cereal").
t: 1 = 2 two-component combinations
2 = 5 two-component combinations
3 = 10 two-component combinations
4 = 20 two-component combinations

d: Given a set of objects or pictures which vary only on a single characteristic, the student will be able to select all of the items which have a single specified characteristic (i.e., adjectives such as "The red ones").
t: 1 = can identify at least one adjective
2 = at least 5 adjectives (may be all colors)
3 = at least 10 adjectives (at least 5 of which are not colors)
4 = selects at least 20 adjectives (including at least 3 colors, 2 shapes, and 2 sizes)

d: Given a varied set of objects or pictures, the student will be able to select all of the items which have the two specified characteristics (e.g., adjectives, parts or other features, function, or class of the item).
t: 1 = 2 two-component combinations
2 = 5 two- component combinations
3 = 10 two-component combinations
4 = 20 two-component combinations

d: The student will be able to select three items in a specified sequence.
t: 1 = accurately selects 2 items in specified sequence after both items are named
2 = accurately selects 3 items in specified sequence after all the items are named

d: The student will be able to follow instructions which include selections involving prepositions.
t: 1 = at least 2 prepositions
2 = at least 3 prepositions
3 = at least 5 prepositions
4 = at least 6 prepositions

d: The student will be able to follow instructions which include selections involving pronouns.
t: 1 = at least 2 pronouns
2 = at least 3
3 = at least 4 pronouns
4 = at least 8 pronouns

d: Student will be able to select pictures of scenes or pictures of activities.
t: 1 = selects at least 2 pictures depicting locations or activties
2 = selects at least 4 pictures depicting locations or activities

d: Student will be able to select pictures of faces depicting various emotions.
t: 1 = at least 1 emotion
2 = at least 2 emotions
